#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `css-only`. [Google guidance](https://m3.material.io/components/lists/overview)

Public JavaScript exports: `Sortable`, `Lists`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: A product with a large image, description, price, and several actions may need a card. A simple product-name index remains a list.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: component.

Support: Standard and segmented lists.

Web adaptation: Native list semantics; visual selection alone does not justify aria-selected.

Known boundary: Lists of single link or button rows move focus with Up, Down, Home and End as a shortcut; rows stay Tab stops, and lists with several controls per row, selection lists and listbox semantics are not provided.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#lists).

#### Contract

Continuous, vertical indexes of text and images. Use a list so people can find an item and act on it. The HTML is the component; the script only adds arrow keys to lists of link or button rows.

The leading visual is the first icon, `<img>`, or `<input>`. The trailing action is the last icon, `<kbd>`, `<button>`, `<time>`, or `.meta`. A following `<p>` is supporting text. Mark the current row with `active` or `selected` — **not** `aria-selected`, which is not valid on a plain `listitem` and needs a role (`option`, `tab`, `row`, `treeitem`) that brings a keyboard contract with it.

Two variants: standard (the default) and `segmented`.

#### Syntax

```html
<ul class="list">
  <li>
    <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">star</span>
    List item
    <kbd>⌘C</kbd>
  </li>
  <li class="selected">
    <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">star</span>
    List item
    <kbd>⌘C</kbd>
  </li>
</ul>
```

#### App behavior

Delete a row at once and offer Undo in a snackbar, as the Snackbar App behavior describes. Ignore the second click of a double click (`event.detail > 1`), or the row that slides up gets deleted too. Before removing a row that holds focus, focus the next row's control, else the previous row's, else the empty state's action. At Undo time, find the row that followed the restored one by id, or put the item back into the data and re-render; don't trust an index or a node taken before other changes. Show the list's empty state when the last row goes, and hide it and update any count when Undo brings a row back.

#### Also documented

The Lists section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Standard, Segmented, Text, Icons, Links, Sortable, Long lists.

#### Rules

- `list-item-not-selected`: aria-selected is not valid on a listitem. A plain <ul> has nowhere to put it - either give the item a role that takes it (option, tab, row, treeitem) and implement that role’s keyboard contract, or drop the attribute.
- `sortable-items-move-without-dragging`: Give each .sortable item a [data-move="up"] and a [data-move="down"] button, in the row or in a menu. Dragging is a pointer gesture; the buttons are the keyboard path and the single-pointer alternative WCAG 2.5.7 requires.
- `list-unstyled-has-list-role`: WebKit drops the list role from a list with no markers, so screen readers stop announcing it as a list. Give a .list-unstyled list role="list", or the role it should have instead.
